author: "Ashqul Islam"

output: pdf_document

The following analysis represents an independent reconstruction of Figures 5B, 5C, and 5D
from the listed publication:
Faith DR, Kinnersley M, Brooks DM, Drecktrah D, Hall LS, Luo E, et al. (2024) 
Characterization and genomic analysis of the Lyme disease spirochete bacteriophage phiBB-1. 
PLoS Pathog 20(4): e1012122. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.ppat.1012122

Publicly available sequencing data found under the journal article was used to
generate tables that were then visualized using ggplot2 to replicate the original figures.

This was done as a final bioinformatics project for an independent study at the Qiu lab at 
CUNY Hunter College for a Biology MA.

Sequence alignment and filtering according to the methods of the publication
can be found in the seqpipe.sh script.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r library, ref and tsv1 setup, message = FALSE}
setwd("/Users/ashqulislam/Desktop/QiuLab/BB1 Figure Project/")
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
#Open reference, idx, and coverage files
ref <- read_tsv("reference_lookup_tabs.tsv",
                col_names = c("Reference", "Replicon"))

kable(ref,
      caption = "Reference Table",
      booktabs = TRUE)

aln1f_idx <- read_tsv("aln1_filtered_idxstats.tsv",
                     col_names = c("Reference", 
                                   "Length", 
                                   "Mapped_Reads", 
                                   "Unmapped_Reads"))

#Removed an unknown tab that wasn't tied to Chromosome or plasmids
#Aligned the reference_lookup tsv which had the replicon names aligned to Reference
aln1f_idx <- aln1f_idx |>
  filter (Reference != "*") |>
  left_join(ref, by = "Reference")

# Rearranged rows to account for left_join
aln1f_idx <- aln1f_idx |>
  select(Reference, Replicon, everything())
#The Chromosome section had multiple rows, assumed it took several reads to 
#cover it. whole_row1 is the isolation of the rows via filter and then summarize
#to condense values. Due to multiple rows encompassing one variable, values are summed.

#ref table and tsv's lists chromosome as "whole". 
#Renamed to "chromosome" for readability

whole_row1f <- aln1f_idx |>
  filter(Replicon == "whole") |>
  summarize(
    Reference = "Chromosome",
    Length = sum(Length),
    Mapped_Reads = sum(Mapped_Reads),
    Unmapped_Reads = sum(Unmapped_Reads),
    Replicon = "chromosome")

#Bind the row back to aln1_idx
aln1f_idx <- aln1f_idx |>
  filter(Replicon != "whole") |>
  bind_rows(whole_row1f)

kable(aln1f_idx,
      caption = "Idxstats table following modifications.",
      booktabs = TRUE)

#Coverage file needed a rename. Followed by a join of ref tsv along with
#reordering the columns

aln1f_cov <- read_tsv("aln1_filtered_coverage.tsv",
                     comment = "")

kable(aln1f_cov,
      caption =  "Coverage Table 1 Unedited",
      booktabs = TRUE)

aln1f_cov<-aln1f_cov |>
  rename(Reference = '#rname')
aln1f_cov <- aln1f_cov |>
  left_join(ref, by = "Reference")|>
  select(Reference, Replicon, everything())

#Chromosome row summarize again but for coverage file. Temporary copies of endpos
#and numreads were used to prevent errors during weights.
#Weights could conflict with sum calculations due to length mismatch. 
#Weighted means in respect to numreads to account for variability

whole_row11f <- aln1f_cov |>
  filter(Replicon == "whole")|>
  mutate(
    fragment_length = endpos,
    fragment_reads = numreads
  )

whole_row11f <- whole_row11f |>
  summarize(
    Reference = "Chromosome",
    Replicon = "chromosome",
    startpos = mean(startpos),
    endpos = sum(endpos),
    numreads = sum(numreads),
    covbases = sum(covbases),
    coverage = weighted.mean(x =coverage, 
                             w = fragment_length),
    meandepth = weighted.mean(x = meandepth, 
                              w = fragment_length),
    meanbaseq = weighted.mean(x = meanbaseq, 
                              w = fragment_reads),
    meanmapq = weighted.mean(x = meanmapq, 
                             w = fragment_reads)
  )
aln1f_cov <- aln1f_cov |>
  filter(Replicon != "whole")|>
  bind_rows(whole_row11f)

#coverage table with relevant columns, ref tabled joined in, summarized chromosome

aln1f_cov |>
  select(Reference, Replicon, endpos, numreads, coverage, meandepth, meanmapq)|>
  kable(
    caption = "Replicate 1 coverage table post-changes.",
    booktabs = TRUE)
```

This process is replicated for tsvs 2 and 3. A final coverage table will be
included for visualization but the code will be hidden during Knit.

```{r cov_all setup, message= FALSE}
#Combine all coverage tables, include replicate numbers

aln1f_cov <- aln1f_cov |>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 1")
aln2f_cov <- aln2f_cov |>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 2")
aln3f_cov <- aln3f_cov |>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 3")
cov_allf <- bind_rows (aln1f_cov, aln2f_cov, aln3f_cov)

#Calculate percent reads for Figure 5B and remove grouping

cov_allf <- cov_allf |>
  group_by(Replicate) |>
  mutate(percent_reads = numreads / sum(numreads) *100)|>
  ungroup()

#An arrangement of replicon order to match publication figures

replicon_order <- c("cp32-1", "cp32-3", "cp32-5", "cp32-10", "cp32-13",
                    "chromosome", "lp54", "cp26", "lp17", "lp36-28-4", "lp38",
                    "lp56", "lp28-3")

```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message = FALSE}
cov_allf |>
  select(Reference, Replicon, endpos, numreads, coverage, meandepth, meanmapq,Replicate)|>
  head(15)|>
  kable(caption = "Shortened Combined Coverage Table",
        booktabs = TRUE)
```

```{r Figure B, message= FALSE}

#calculate a mean percent read and se based off all replicates

figBf_summary <- cov_allf |>
  group_by(Replicon) |>
  summarize(
    mean_percent = mean(percent_reads),
    se_percent = sd(percent_reads)/sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Replicon = factor(Replicon, levels = replicon_order))

#setup to include replicates

cov_all_plot <- cov_allf |>
  mutate(
    Replicate = factor(
      Replicate,
      levels = c("Replicate 1", "Replicate 2", "Replicate 3")
    ),
    Replicon = factor(Replicon, levels = replicon_order)
    )

figB <- ggplot(data = figBf_summary)+
  aes(x = Replicon, y = mean_percent)+
  coord_cartesian(xlim = NULL, ylim = c(0,45))+
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% reads")+
  theme_classic(base_size = 18)+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0))+ #remove offset on x-axis
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.2),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust =1, size = 16)
  )+
  geom_col(
    fill = "royalblue4",
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_percent - se_percent,
      ymax = mean_percent + se_percent))+
  geom_point(
    data = cov_all_plot,
    aes(x = Replicon, y = percent_reads, shape = Replicate),
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.05,
                                    dodge.width = 0.5), #prevent replicate overlap
    size = 3,
    fill = "gray80",
    color = "black",
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +
   scale_shape_manual(
     values = c(
       "Replicate 1" = 21,
       "Replicate 2" = 22,
       "Replicate 3" = 24 #manually include replicate shapes
     )
   )
```

```{r Figure 5C}
#installed ggbreak here. Removed for rmd
#install.packages ("ggbreak")
library(ggbreak)
#same process as Figure 5B
figCf_summary <- cov_allf |>
  group_by(Replicon) |>
  summarize(
    mean_depth = mean(meandepth),
    se_depth = sd(meandepth)/sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Replicon = factor(Replicon, levels = replicon_order))

#scale_y_break used to replicate broken y axis in original figure
#Unable to fix x-axis offset due to it being an artifact of ggbreak

figC <- ggplot(data = figCf_summary)+
  aes(x = Replicon, y = mean_depth)+
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean Coverage")+
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0),
                     breaks = c(0, 20, 75, 150, 1000, 3000, 5000),
                     limits = c(0, 5000))+
  scale_y_break(c(150, 900),
                scales = 0.3,
                space = 0.8)+
  theme_classic(base_size = 18)+
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.2),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust =1, size = 16),
    axis.line.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y.right = element_blank(), #removed a right-sided y-axis
    panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines")
    )+
  geom_col(
    fill = "royalblue4",
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 20,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "orange",
    linewidth = 0.8
  )+
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_depth - se_depth,
      ymax = mean_depth + se_depth),
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 0.8 
    )+
  geom_point(
    data = cov_all_plot,
    aes(x = Replicon, y = meandepth, shape = Replicate),
    size = 3,
    fill = "gray80",
    color = "black",
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +
   scale_shape_manual(
     values = c(
       "Replicate 1" = 21,
       "Replicate 2" = 22,
       "Replicate 3" = 24
     )
   )
```

```{r setup for Figure 5D, message=FALSE}
read_1 <- read_tsv("aln1_read_lengths.tsv")|>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 1")
read_2 <- read_tsv("aln2_read_lengths.tsv")|>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 2")
read_3 <- read_tsv("aln3_read_lengths.tsv")|>
  mutate(Replicate = "Replicate 3")
reads_all <- bind_rows(read_1,
                       read_2,
                       read_3)
reads_all <- left_join(reads_all, ref, by = "Reference")
reads_all <- reads_all |>
  mutate(Replicon = recode(Replicon,
                           "whole" = "chromosome"))
reads_all <- reads_all |>
  mutate(Replicon = factor(Replicon, levels = replicon_order))

#Preview of reads_all

reads_all|>
  head(17)|>
  kable(caption = "Raw Read Table 17/58k rows",
        booktabs=TRUE)

```

```{r Figure 5D, message = FALSE}

#No replicates, all three long-read runs were likely combined

figD <- ggplot(data = reads_all)+
  aes(x = Replicon, y = ReadLength)+
  coord_cartesian(xlim = NULL, ylim = c(0,100000))+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = 0)+
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Read Length")+
  theme_classic(base_size = 18)+
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 1.2),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 1.2),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 55, hjust =1, size = 16))+
  geom_violin(
    adjust = 0.7,
    scale = "width",
    trim = TRUE,
    width = 0.7,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    draw_quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
    fill = "royalblue4",
    color = "black") #adjust, scale, trim, and width for improved visualization
```

Full Analysis of reconstructions can be found in the BIOL792.02_phiBB1_report.
Generally, the reproduced figures seem to match the same trends observed in the 
original publication. Differences may be due to differences in methods and
tools used at certain steps and a lack of access to the original source code.
